title: been working on a phishing link detector, the false positives were way harder than i thought
description: This content discusses the development of a phishing URL detector focused on identifying phishing attempts based solely on URL text analysis. The detector achieves about 90% detection on unseen phishing URLs but struggles with false positives and phishing hosted on compromised legitimate sites. It highlights challenges such as phishing URLs hosted on trusted domains like docs.google.com and the difficulty of blocking such domains outright. The tool is open source and intended as a learning resource rather than an active threat report.

references.title: Reddit Discussion: been working on a phishing link detector, the false positives were way harder than i thought

aiSummary: The post describes the creation of a phishing URL detection tool trained on approximately 15,000 verified phishing URLs from PhishTank. It identifies common phishing tactics including use of trusted domains (e.g., docs.google.com), URL obfuscation techniques (e.g., punycode, misleading subdomains), and look-alike domains. The detector analyzes URL text only, without visiting sites, and flags URLs with explanations. False positives were a significant challenge, requiring tuning to maintain a false alarm rate under 2%. The tool detects about 90% of phishing URLs it has not previously seen but is less effective against phishing hosted on hacked legitimate sites. The author shares the tool and methodology openly for educational purposes.
aiImpact: The content does not describe a specific vulnerability or active threat but rather a detection tool and its limitations. The impact is primarily educational, providing insights into phishing URL characteristics and detection challenges. There is no direct exploitation or compromise described.
